If a comment containing backticks is encountered, and the grammar isn't careful to distinguish comment vs string vs template string contexts, a parsing error occurs leaving the template literal tokenization "open".

- If a comment contains a backtick (\`), and the template-string pattern is "greedy" or misordered (matching even inside comments), it can break the tokenization. This means the `template-string` pattern may be picking up text inside comments, or forgetting to reset itself after errors, etc.

The most probable location is the `template-string` pattern in `components/prism-javascript.js` where the regex is defined as greedy. This can cause template literals inside comments to interfere with following lines.
